data.caption: Ricaricati mentre dormi!
data.copy:
"Mi hanno diagnosticato l'insonnia a 42 anni. Adesso ne ho 51. Si scopre che il mio problema era elettrico.

Per nove anni ho "gestito" un disturbo che non avevo davvero.

Nove anni di melatonina che mi lasciava intontita ogni mattina.

Nove anni di trazodone che mi stendeva — ma non mi faceva mai riposare davvero.

Nove anni di nuove ricette in mano e dottori che mi dicevano di "ottimizzare l'igiene del sonno".

Ho fatto tutto quello che mi hanno chiesto.

Ho tolto l'alcol. Poi il caffè della mattina. Poi la caffeina del tutto.

Ho preso la melatonina. 1 mg. Poi 3 mg. Poi 10 mg. Poi ha smesso di funzionare.

Ho provato magnesio, L-teanina, GABA, ashwagandha, CBD.

Ho fatto terapia cognitivo-comportamentale specifica per l'insonnia — 150 euro a seduta — perché la mia dottoressa diceva che era la cosa più documentata in circolazione.

Ha aiutato un po'. Per un periodo.

Poi non più.

Quando ha smesso di funzionare, mi hanno mandata a un centro del sonno.

Due notti attaccata a dei fili mentre una telecamera mi guardava fissare il soffitto.

Polisonnografia. Inconcludente.

Mi hanno controllato per le apnee notturne. Negativo.

Sindrome delle gambe senza riposo. No.

Tiroide. Normale.

Esami del sangue. Perfetti.

"Va tutto bene", mi ha detto lo specialista. "È solo insonnia cronica. Abbiamo escluso tutto il resto."

Mi ha consegnato un'altra ricetta e mi ha detto di tornare tra tre mesi.

Mi sentivo come se stessi impazzendo.

Gli esami erano normali. I medici non erano preoccupati. Ma ogni singola notte, il mio corpo si rifiutava di dormire.

Verso le 21 iniziava il terrore. Sapevo già come sarebbe andata la notte.

Alle 22 ero a letto, a fissare il soffitto, completamente sveglia.

A mezzanotte iniziavo a fare i conti.

Se mi addormento adesso, dormo sei ore.
Se mi addormento adesso, ne dormo cinque.
Se mi addormento adesso…

Mi svegliavo alle 3 di notte senza un motivo. Cuore già a mille. Testa che già macinava la giornata di domani come se dovesse…

data.caption: Read this if you want your libido back
data.copy:
Someone put a horny teenage boy inside my 57-year-old body. My poor husband is exhausted. I've been going at him three times a day for two months and I refuse to apologise.

I need to explain how a woman who hadn't wanted sex in six years ended up here. Because if you'd told me last Christmas this is where I'd be, I'd have laughed and then probably cried.

I'm Catherine. 57. Married 27 years to a man I'm lucky to have. Two grown kids out of the house. A life that, from the outside, anyone would say is working.

Menopause turned up at 51 and switched something off inside me that I didn't know was switchable. It wasn't gradual. It wasn't a dimming. It was more like a fuse blowing in a part of the house you only noticed once it went dark. Whatever the part of me was that used to hum when my husband walked past... that bit stopped working. Overnight.

I went to see my GP about it. Every friend I had was on HRT by then, talking about patches and gels the way people talk about finding a parking space right outside Waitrose. I wanted in.

My GP brought up my file. She scrolled. She stopped scrolling.

What she saw was the thing I'd put behind me three years earlier. Breast cancer at 48. The oestrogen-fed kind. I'd done the surgery, the radiation, the five years of Tamoxifen. I'd rung the bell. I'd moved on. Except the hospital hadn't, because on paper I was still a woman whose cancer had eaten oestrogen for breakfast.

"You can't have HRT, Catherine. Not with your history. I'm really sorry."

I held it together. Thanked her. Got to the car before it came out of me in a single ugly sob. A woman my age was walking her spaniel past the surgery and she turned her head, pretending she hadn't seen, which was kind of her.

Here's what I want you to understand about the part that came next. It wasn't the sex I missed most. It was being someone who wanted things.

data.caption: For the women Berberine does not cooperate with.
data.copy:
I cried in the Walgreens Imodium aisle in May.

I am 49 years old. I have a husband, two teenagers, and a job I have been at for 14 years. And I was standing in the digestive aisle of a Walgreens at 2:30 in the afternoon, holding a 30-count box of anti-diarrheal medication, buying it so I could keep taking the supplement that was supposed to fix my perimenopause weight gain.

That was the day I admitted Berberine was not the answer.

If you are reading this and you have ever bought Imodium specifically so you could keep taking Berberine — if "Nature's Ozempic" has turned into a part-time job of bathroom logistics — this is the article I needed someone to put in front of me three months earlier.

I tried what felt like everything before Berberine. None of it worked the way it was supposed to. Berberine was just the latest in a long line, and Berberine was the one that finally made me sit down and ask the question nobody had been asking. Including me.

---

Let me tell you what I had tried before I ended up in that drugstore aisle.

I am not someone who jumps on supplements. I read first. I wait. I have a notebook in my kitchen drawer where I keep track of what works and what does not. By the time I bought Berberine, the notebook was almost full.

It started in the spring of 2022, when I was 47 and my jeans had stopped fitting for the second year in a row. I had not changed how I ate. I had not stopped exercising. The weight came on anyway, mostly through my middle, the way my mother's had at exactly the same age.

The first thing I did was cut alcohol. I had been having two glasses of wine four nights a week. I cut to nothing for three months. Lost zero pounds.

Then I cut sugar. No dessert. No sweetened coffee. No granola bars. Three more months. Lost two pounds, gained them back the week of my husband's birthday.

data.copy:
For ex-vapers who quit, but can't stop wondering what they already did to their lungs.

I was carrying groceries up two flights when I felt it.

Not much. A tightness. Three seconds at the top of the stairs.

That was nothing. But the thought that came with it, before I even set the bags down, that wasn't nothing.

Is this healing? Or is this damage?

I'd quit vaping eight months earlier. I was proud of that. The cravings were brutal and I got through them and I'd been telling myself the hard part was over.

It wasn't.

Here's what no one says about quitting.

The quit doesn't close the question. It opens a different one.

Because once the vape is gone, you're alone with your body. Your body does things you don't remember it doing. And you can't tell if that means you're healing, or if you already crossed a line you can't come back from.

I vaped every day for four years. Disposables, mostly. The kind that just live in your hand. I didn't think of it as smoking. I thought it was lighter than that. Something I could put down whenever I felt like it.

I was wrong.

Four years of all-day vaping, and now I'm standing at the top of two flights of stairs wondering if I started a countdown that's already running.

That question doesn't wait.

It's on the bus. It's at midnight. Right here at the top of the stairs with groceries in my hands. And once it arrives, I can't make it go away.

I started doing things I'm embarrassed to say out loud.

Every night before bed I'd take a slow deep breath and try to feel if the air hit the bottom of my lungs. Testing it. Comparing it to how it felt a year ago. Two years ago. Before.

I'd read something once: "It took me about 10 days to feel the air hit the bottom of my lungs again." I turned that into a test I ran every single night.

Most nights I couldn't feel the bottom.

data.copy:
Ich höre gerne Podcasts beim Einschlafen.

Eines Nachts, es war 2 Uhr, ich konnte nicht schlafen wegen der Krämpfe, habe ich einen über das Darmmikrobiom gehört.

Darin sagte ein Gastroenterologe etwas, das mich aufrecht sitzen ließ:

"Die chronischen Beschwerden die wir als 'funktionell' oder 'stressbedingt' abtun. Blähbauch, Müdigkeit, Brain Fog, diffuse Gelenkschmerzen, werden in der modernen Forschung zunehmend mit einem einzigen gemeinsamen Nenner in Verbindung gebracht: dem Zustand des Darmmikrobioms. Das Problem ist, dass Hausärzte das nicht messen. Sie messen Blut. Aber Blut zeigt das meistens nicht."

Ich habe am nächsten Morgen diesen Podcast an meine Ärztin geschickt.

Sie hat nie geantwortet.

Mein Name ist Stefanie. Ich bin 46 Jahre alt und ich lebe in Hamburg.

Meine Beschwerden begannen mit 38. Ich erinnere mich noch gut: Es war kurz nach einem zweiwöchigen Antibiotika-Kurs wegen einer hartnäckigen Bronchitis. Danach, ich kann keinen anderen Zeitpunkt benennen, hat sich mein Körper verändert.

Lebensmittel die ich jahrzehntelang ohne Probleme gegessen hatte plötzlich nicht mehr vertragen. Blähungen die sich aufbauten wie Wetterfronten. Ein tägliches Brain Fog das sich anfühlte wie Watte im Kopf. Erschöpfung die nicht mit Schlaf besser wurde.

Ich habe meinen Hausarzt aufgesucht. Blutbild: normal. Schilddrüse: normal. Entzündungswerte: normal. Zöliakie-Test: negativ.

"Es könnte Reizdarm sein. Versuchen Sie, Stress zu reduzieren."

Sechs Monate später: dieselben Symptome. Neue Ärztin. Neues Blutbild. Gleiche Ergebnisse. "Haben Sie schon Magnesium versucht?"

Ein Jahr später: Gastroenterologin. Koloskopie: "Strukturell alles in Ordnung." Endoskopie: "Schleimhaut unauffällig." Diagnose: "IBS-M. Management durch Diät."

Ich habe Low-FODMAP probiert. Ich war so eingeschränkt in dem was ich essen durfte, dass ich aufgehört habe, mit meinen Freunden essen zu gehen. Ich habe Tupperware-Gerichte zu Geburtstagsdinnern mitgenommen. …

data.copy:
My dad died of lung cancer at 56. I watched it happen. Three years later vaping nearly killed me the exact same way.
I'm James Carter. 41. Sheffield. Joiner.

Not a doctor. Not a "wellness expert." Not some startup bro with a podcast.

I'm just the bloke who built a non-nicotine inhaler in his shed because the NHS quit-smoking service couldn't help me, the patches couldn't help me, and my GP told me — in those EXACT words — "you've just got to want it more."

Want it more.

Right.

After 27 years smoking and 4 years vaping, I wanted it so much my chest was caving in.

Let me tell you what actually happened.

Sunday. 3am. Sat in my kitchen with my heart hammering so loud I could hear it in my ears, certain I was about to drop dead exactly the way my father did.

I wasn't.

What I was, was completely addicted to a Lost Mary I'd been pulling on for 14 hours straight.

Monday morning I rang my GP. Emergency appointment. ECG fine. Bloods fine. He gave me a leaflet.

A LEAFLET.

That afternoon I sat in my shed and cried for the first time since dad's funeral.

Then I started reading.

Real research. Behavioural addiction studies. Neurobiology papers. Stuff most GPs haven't got the time to look at.

What I learned changed everything.

⚠️ It's not the nicotine. It's the LOOP.

Hand. Mouth. Breath. 200 times a day for years until your brain literally can't do anything else.

Patches give you nicotine WITHOUT the loop = your brain rejects it.
Gum gives you nicotine WITHOUT the loop = your brain rejects it.

So I built the OPPOSITE.

Solid walnut. Hand-turned in my shed in Sheffield. No nicotine. No vapour. No batteries. Just the loop your brain has been begging for — without the poison that comes with it.

I tested it on myself first. 19 months vape-free.

Then I gave one to my brother. He stopped in 11 days.

Then his mate. Then my wife's cousin.

Then 22,000 other Brits.

I'm still not a doctor. I'm still a joiner. I'm just a Sheffield bloke who didn't want to die…

data.caption: For women over 50 who know the frozen shoulder night ache and do not want to lose another year.
data.copy:
"I don't even wanna think about it."

That's what I said out loud in the kitchen last Tuesday. To nobody. Just me and the coffee pot.

Because the other shoulder. The LEFT one. The one that was supposed to be fine.

It's started.

I've been hiding from it for about three weeks now. Telling myself it's nothing. Telling myself I slept on it wrong. Telling myself that reaching for the cereal shelf hurt because my posture is off, because I'm tense, because I'm carrying groceries with the "good" side and compensating.

Lies. All of them. I know this feeling. I've felt this feeling before.

The dull ache under the deltoid. The weird tightness when I reach across my body. The tiny catch when I put on a seatbelt. The SAME sequence I had 14 months ago on the right side.

And I have spent 14 months getting the right side back. Fourteen months. Three PTs. Two cortisone shots. A dry needling lady who charged me $180 a session and told me it would resolve with "time and movement."

It did not resolve with time and movement.

It resolved with something else. I'll get to that.

But last Tuesday I was pouring coffee and I reached for the creamer and I felt the zinger. The actual zinger. Not a twinge. A zinger. That shock that takes your breath. On the LEFT side. The side that was supposed to be untouched.

And I said out loud, "I don't even wanna think about it."

Because thinking about it means admitting it. And admitting it means another 14 months. Another $4,000 in treatments that don't work. Another winter of sleeping with three pillows stacked under the bad arm. Another Christmas of not decorating the tree.

I can't do that again. I can't. I will not survive another 14 months of this.

So I'm writing this because if you are reading this and the second shoulder has started, you need to stop hiding from it the way I was hiding from it. I was wasting time I didn't have.

Here is what I learned. And I learned it too late for the first shoulder and just in time for the second.

data.caption: Your reading the wrong bible...
data.copy:
Genesis 6:4 reads "The Nephilim were on the earth in those days and—also afterward—when the sons of God went to the daughters of humans and had children by them. They were the heroes of old, men of renown."

Moses writes that in the time of Noah, the Nephilim were on the Earth. It's the 6th chapter in arguably the most important book of the Bible. Then, right after this, we're introduced to God's plan to flood the Earth and wipe it clean from all the "evil."

The craziest part of this verse is the "and also afterward." Implying the Nephilim are STILL on earth to this day, not in physical, but spiritual form.

Genesis 6:6-7 then says, "The Lord saw how great the wickedness of the human race had become on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was only evil all the time. The Lord regretted that he had made human beings on the earth, and his heart was deeply troubled."

Then, we're introduced to the parallel of Enoch and Noah. We learn Enoch walked with God, how Noah was blameless, what the Nephilim were, then immediately after, the Great Flood.

Genesis 5:24: "Enoch walked faithfully with God; then he was no more, because God took him away." Genesis 6:9: "Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked faithfully with God."

I always thought how weird it was that Enoch walked with God, but his book wasn't included in the King James Bible. I knew the reason too. They weren't able to prove it to be authentic.

But, when I saw this Joe Rogan clip with biblical scholar Wes Huff, my perspective shifted a bit. Joe said,

"I had Representative Anna Paulina on the podcast, and she was talking to me about the Book of Enoch. She said it wasn't included in the Bible because a bunch of jewish rabbis said it didn't align with the Torah, so they yanked it out. But it's an original biblical text, they found it in the Dead Sea Scrolls."

I heard this and my first thought was "I don't need any other books... missing…

data.caption: Läs detta om det känns omöjligt att sluta med nässpray☝
data.copy:
Till dig som har varit fast i nässpraycykeln i mer än tre år och har sagt till dig själv att du ska ta tag i det ordentligt någon gång, bara inte just nu…

Vävnaden väntar inte på rätt tillfälle den heller. Rhinitis medicamentosa orsakar en gradvis nedbrytning av slemhinnan, en process som går att återställa på cellnivå under de första åren, men betydligt mindre ju längre cykeln pågår. Var du befinner dig i den utvecklingen är värt att veta innan du avgör när rätt tillfälle är.

Det rätta tillfället hade varit på väg i ungefär fyra år.

Det var alltid nästan här. Precis efter att det nuvarande projektet var klart. När jobbet blev lite mindre krävande. När jag hade utrymme att må ordentligt dåligt så länge det skulle ta att sluta.

Jag hade flaskan på nattduksbordet och sa till mig själv att jag var en person som skulle ta tag i det här, bara inte den här veckan, inte den här månaden, inte just nu.

Det finns en särskild kvalitet i ett beroende som helt har smält in i vardagen. Det slutar kännas som en kris och börjar kännas som en variabel. Något du planerar runt på samma sätt som du planerar runt andra fasta delar av dagen. Jag visste vilka apotek nära mitt jobb som hade öppet sent. Jag packade inför helger annorlunda än andra, inte mer, bara med en specifik sak som inte fick glömmas bort på samma sätt som annat kunde glömmas. Jag hade slutat reagera på flaskan på nattduksbordet som något som inte borde vara där. Den bara var där, som andra saker bara är där.

Jag sa till mig själv att det här var kontroll. Att hantera det ansvarsfullt medan jag väntade på rätt tillfälle var en rimlig hållning.

Det slog mig aldrig att vävnaden hade en annan relation till tid än jag hade.

Anpassningen sker så gradvis att du inte ser formen av den förrän du försöker beskriva den för någon som inte har levt i den.

Jag hade slutat boka vissa typer av resor. Inte medvetet, inte som ett beslut ja…

data.caption: kinderspeech.sk
data.copy:
Hneď ako som si na kontrole vypočula slová „oneskorený vývin reči," logopédka dodala: „Ale nebojte sa, ešte máte čas to DOHNAŤ." Nikto mi ale nepovedal, ŽE ten čas beží rýchlejšie, ako si myslíte – a čo presne mám robiť, kým ešte neuplynul.

Zapísala to do karty. OVR. Tri písmená. Oneskorený vývin reči.

Kývla som hlavou, obliekla Sofinku a odišla. V aute som si to zopakovala. „Ešte máte čas." Dobre. Čas mám. Všetko bude v poriadku.

Ale keď som v ten večer ukladala Sofinku do postieľky a povedala „daj pusinku mami," ona sa na mňa len pozrela. Žiadna pusinka. Žiadne „mami." Len veľké hnedé oči a ticho.

Osemnásť mesiacov. Jedno slovo. „Ham." A aj to len niekedy.

Otvorila som telefón a napísala do vyhľadávača: „OVR 18 mesiacov skúsenosti."

To bola moja prvá chyba. Nie preto, že som hľadala. Ale preto, že som našla stovky príbehov – a KAŽDÝ bol iný. Jedna mamička písala, že jej syn prehovoril v troch a dnes je úplne v poriadku. Ďalšia písala, že čakala a v štyroch rokoch dostali diagnózu PAS.

A ja som nevedela, ktorý príbeh bude ten náš.

O pol dvanástej v noci som googlila „kritické okno pre vývin reči." A tam som prvýkrát natrafila na číslo, ktoré mi nikto nepovedal.

Osemnásť až tridsaťšesť mesiacov. To je to okno. Obdobie, keď mozog vytvára najintenzívnejšie nervové spojenia pre reč. Keď sa dráhy medzi uchom, mozgom a ústami spájajú najrýchlejšie. A potom sa to spomalí. Nezastaví – spomalí. Ale každý mesiac po tridsiatom šiestom stojí dvojnásobné, trojnásobné úsilie.

Sofi mala osemnásť mesiacov. Práve jej to okno začalo.

A ja som v ňom stála s jediným plánom: „počkajte."

V tú noc som nespala do tretej. Nie od strachu. Od hnevu. Lebo „ešte máte čas" nie je plán. Je to veta, ktorou vás pošlú domov, aby ste sa necítili zle. Ale nikto vám nepovie, čo máte robiť POČAS toho čakania. Koľko slov den…
data.description: Pridajte sa k stovkám rodičov, ktorí pomáhajú svojim deťom nájsť svoj hlas! Stovky spokojných slovenských rodičov a detí používajú naše produkty každý deň. Ďakujeme za dôveru!❤️ Prečítajte si naše recenzie, v ktorých mnohí rodičia vyjadrujú svoje pozitívne skúsenost...

keyword.description: Free-text search string (lowercased server-side). Use for product names, brands, hooks, domains — not for category/niche (use niches).
keyword.allowed_values: Any string; empty = no text filter.

searchkeyword.description: Which ad field keyword searches. NOT a niche/category selector.
searchkeyword.allowed_values: All, landingurl, pagename, adtext, productname. Default All when keyword is set.

countries.description: Ad target countries (where the ad runs — wlads.countries). Not store HQ.
countries.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated ISO2: US, GB, DK, NL, BE, IE, NO, SE, FR, DE, IT, CA, NZ, AU, BR, AT, CH, ES, FI, PL, PT, GR, TR, AE, SA, QA, KW, BH, OM, JO, IL, LB, IQ, EG.
countries.notes: MX/CO/CL are not in this Meta targeting catalog. Use store_based_in for stores based in those markets.

excludeCountries.allowed_values: Comma-separated ISO2: US, GB, DK, NL, BE, IE, NO, SE, FR, DE, IT, CA, NZ, AU, BR, AT, CH, ES, FI, PL, PT, GR, TR, AE, SA, QA, KW, BH, OM, JO, IL, LB, IQ, EG.

storebasedin.description: Store Based In (dashboard storebasedin → store_traffic.shop_origin_country). Use for Mexico/Colombia/Chile/etc. store HQ.
storebasedin.allowed_values: Comma-separated ISO2 including MX, CO, CL, AR, PE and other Explore Shops Based In markets.

niches.description: Product category / vertical filter (dashboard Meta niches). Use when user asks for a category, niche, vertical, or market — not keyword.
niches.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated codes: CG, AM, GG, JY, GS, HT, BY, BG, SK, WC, MC, SP, KS, TS, HE, PS, DP, HI, FT, OG, OP, TR, AC, AA, BM, FK, SH, SW, EL, FW, WT, EW, FR, GM, PH, EC, WE, SC, BE, MU, PA, CB, CF, CP, DC, CT, HH, SG, YG, CC, PZ, LS, GP, WN, SF, OR, MG, PB. See allowed_niches in response for code→label map. Fashion/clothing = CG.

website.description: Detected store/checkout technology on the landing page (dashboard Website filter).
website.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated codes: SH, TP, BU, LS, CC, SL, TA, GG, FU, CS, LP, FO, SI, GP, XS, YC, HY, DI, MS, SB, PP, WC, TT, TW, PI, GO, SC, FB, MG, WP, SQ, PS, GM, KV, CO, HJ, WX, AR, BC, MC. SH=Shopify, WC=WooCommerce, CS=Clickfunnels. See allowed_technologies in response.

languages.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated: en, nl, de, no, fr, sv, da, it, pt, es, fi, pl, tr, ar, he.

excludeLanguages.allowed_values: Comma-separated: en, nl, de, no, fr, sv, da, it, pt, es, fi, pl, tr, ar, he.

apps.description: Shopify apps detected on the store.
apps.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated app names/ids from dashboard Apps filter. See allowed_apps in response.

excludeApps.description: Exclude stores using these Shopify apps.
excludeApps.allowed_values: Comma-separated app names/ids. See allowed_apps in response.

themes.description: Shopify theme name on the store (exact match).
themes.allowed_values: All, or comma-separated exact theme names from dashboard Themes filter (discover via GET /api/themes).

scaling.allowed_values: rising, stable, declining, nodownscaling, upscaling, downscaling.

mediafilter.allowed_values: videos, images, carousel, dco. Omit/All = all formats.

pagetypefilter.allowed_values: products, collections, funnels, nofunnels. Empty/All = all types.

adscorefilter.description: WinningHunter ad score tier (Established / Has Potential / Unestablished).
adscorefilter.allowed_values: winning (Established), scaling (Has Potential), testing (Unestablished). Requires matching account tier.

lowimpressions.description: Hide ads with very low impressions.
lowimpressions.allowed_values: hide (exclude low-impression rows). Omit = show all.

rankgrowthfilter.description: Within-brand ad rank momentum vs historic rank_history.
rankgrowthfilter.allowed_values: Comma-separated subset of: rising, stable, declining.

minadrank.description: Minimum within-brand ad rank (lower rank number = stronger ad for that brand, e.g. #1).

min.description: Minimum duplicate/active-seen ad count on the page.

minactiveads.description: Minimum active Meta ads on the advertiser Facebook page (total_active_ads_on_page).
minactiveads.notes: find_winning_products auto-applies minactiveads=50 for US when not set (see forced block).

minactiveadsgrowth.description: Minimum page active-ads percent growth over activeadsgrowthperiod.
minactiveadsgrowth.allowed_values: Human percent (25 = 25%); negatives allowed for decline.

activeadsgrowthperiod.description: Lookback window for active-ads growth filter.
activeadsgrowthperiod.allowed_values: 1w, 1m, 3m. Default 1m when min/max growth set. 1w=1 week, 1m=1 month, 3m=3 months.
activeadsgrowthperiod.notes: 14d/2m exist on the dashboard but are omitted from MCP — sparse wlads baselines return empty result sets.

minpagelikes.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. Ads missing the field excluded when min set.

minadspend.description: Minimum EU ad spend total in adspendtimeframe window.
minadspend.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier; can return upgrade JSON.

maxadspend.description: Maximum EU ad spend in window.
maxadspend.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. 999999 treated as no upper cap server-side.

adspendtimeframe.description: Rolling window ad spend is summed over (NOT a calendar month filter).

minreach.description: Minimum EU reach/views total in reachtimeframe window.
minreach.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

reachtimeframe.description: Rolling window reach is summed over.

mintraffic.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

minproductsonstore.description: Minimum published products on the Shopify store.

minprice.description: Minimum product price on landing page.

mincopylength.description: Minimum ad primary text character length.

minvideolength.description: Minimum video duration in seconds (use with mediafilter=videos).

mindays.description: Minimum days the ad has been running.
mindays.allowed_values: Integer >= 0. May require higher account tier.

from.description: Ad launch date lower bound (Meta started field — when ad began running, NOT scrape date).
from.allowed_values: YYYY-MM-DD. Requires to on same range.

to.notes: To isolate ads running in a calendar month: ad_created_to=last day of month AND fromlastseen=first day of month.

product_from.description: Shopify product creation date lower bound.

pagefrom.description: Facebook page creation date lower bound.

activestatus.description: Legacy dashboard param (no longer applied to ES queries).
activestatus.allowed_values: Ignored — use adstatus or last_seen_from/to instead.

adstatus.description: Dashboard Status filter — recently seen vs stale ads.
adstatus.allowed_values: active (lastSeen or updated_at within last 4 days), inactive (neither field within last 4 days), All/empty (no status filter).
adstatus.notes: find_winning_products forces active. Same as dashboard Status = Active.

sorting.allowed_values: relevance, datefound, mostrecent, lastseen, adspend, longestrunning, reach, adsetamount, consistency, monthlyvisits, monthlytraffic, monthlyrevenue, pageactiveads, toprank, mostsaved. Aliases: rank/top_ad/best_ranked→toprank (asc = best rank first, desc = worst rank first). ad_started→mostrecent. monthly_visits→monthlyvisits. monthly_traffic→monthlytraffic.

page.description: Pagination page index (informational). Deep pagination requires scroll from the previous response — incrementing page alone does not advance the result set.
page.allowed_values: MCP uses 1-based page (1=first page); echoed value is 0-based internal page sent to API.

scroll.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Empty/omit on the first request; pass the response scroll value on the next request with the same filters to fetch more ads. Required to download beyond the first page (especially sort_by=lastseen).
scroll.allowed_values: Opaque string from previous response; empty string or omit for first page. Stop when scroll is null/absent or data is shorter than a full page.

KB Back In Stock Restock Alert
Sticky Add To Cart Booster Pro
POWR Email Popup Sales Pop Ups
EG Auto Add to Cart Free Gift
SA Request a Quote, Hide Price

Tada Pop up Spin Wheel Popups
Coupon X: Discount Code Pop Up

mcp_pagination.hint: Pass scroll_next as scroll on the next call with the same filters to continue. Do not rely on page alone.
